negative: Attempt a nonattribute declaration inside attribute syntax.
positive: Use an attribute name matching an ordinary identifier without namespace conflict.

edge: Reuse a name in separate sibling block namespaces.
negative: Give a local variable and named block the same name in one block namespace.
positive: Declare distinct local variable and type names in a function.

edge: Contrast same-unit lexical lookup with forbidden package-import and hierarchical access.
negative: Reject importing the compilation-unit scope or reaching one of its declarations by hierarchical path.
positive: Use ordinary same-unit lookup for a compilation-unit declaration without importing its scope.

edge: Use a same-named declaration in another namespace.
positive: Place a package-permitted declaration and bind construct at compilation-unit scope.

negative: Give a compilation-unit variable and type the same name.
positive: Declare distinct kinds with distinct names at compilation-unit scope.

edge: Forward-reference a task or function name under its stated exception.
negative: Reject qualified and unqualified references to a later compilation-unit variable.
positive: Reference an earlier compilation-unit variable, qualified and unqualified.

edge: Compile the same files separately and observe distinct local compilation-unit scopes.
positive: Compile two files as one unit and declare an outermost item belonging to their shared compilation-unit scope.

edge: Shadow a top-level name with a compilation-unit declaration and verify local resolution wins.
negative: Reject the reference when neither local/imported nor a valid rooted hierarchy path exists.
positive: From compilation-unit scope, reference a top-level hierarchy name not shadowed locally and resolve it from $root.

edge: Place a declaration in the first file and reference it from the second.
notes: Invocation syntax is tool-specific; only availability and language effects of both use models are required.
positive: Compile two files once as one unit and once as separate units, observing corresponding name visibility.

edge: Use an error detectable only after parameter computation.
negative: Do not begin simulation before reporting a required compile-time error.
notes: The oracle is the pre-simulation deadline, not an implementation's internal phase boundary.
positive: Report an elaboration-dependent compile-time error after parsing but before simulation.

edge: Select between same-named cells in different libraries.
positive: Use a configuration and library map to select a particular implementation for a module instance.

edge: Contrast a globally visible package with an ordinary item declared at compilation-unit scope.
negative: Reject a source-language name reference to an ordinary compilation-unit-scope variable from another unit.
positive: Reference a module declared in another compilation unit.

edge: Contrast a nested declaration with a nonnested one.
negative: Reuse one global name for a module and interface in different units.
positive: Give different global names to a module and interface across units.

edge: Compile the same files as one unit and separately to observe the permitted semantic difference.
negative: Verify the directive does not leak into a separately compiled unit.
positive: Set a directive in one unit and observe its effect on later text in that unit.

edge: Resolve a path through a parameter-selected generated hierarchy.
negative: Diagnose an unresolved hierarchical path before simulation begins.
positive: Resolve a hierarchical reference to a member of an elaborated child instance.

edge: Bind both an implicit top-level component and an explicitly nested instance.
negative: Diagnose an instance whose referenced design component cannot be bound before simulation starts.
positive: Elaborate a module containing nested module, interface, and primitive instances and observe the resulting instance hierarchy.

edge: Establish connectivity through multiple hierarchy levels.
negative: Diagnose a port connection that cannot establish legal net connectivity before simulation.
positive: Elaborate connected module ports and observe that the resulting nets carry values between instances.

edge: Compute a dependent parameter chain before sizing an elaborated object.
negative: Diagnose a parameter expression that cannot be validly computed for elaboration.
positive: Override a parameter and observe an elaborated width derived from its computed value.

edge: Use all four argument directions in one function declaration.
positive: Define and call functions using each of input, output, inout, and ref arguments.

edge: Fork a process from a function and allow the forked process, rather than the function execution, to block time.
negative: Reject a function body that directly blocks simulation time.
positive: Call a function that returns in the current simulation time.

edge: Call both forms from the same procedural context.
negative: Reject using a void function call as an expression operand.
positive: Use a nonvoid function call in an expression and call a void function as a statement.

edge: Provide the minimum via each of the three specification forms in turn.
positive: Use several precision sources and verify simulation advances at the finest precision.

edge: Reference both upward and downward across multiple levels.
negative: Reject a hierarchical path with a nonexistent component.
positive: Reference a nested instance member from a different hierarchy branch using a full hierarchical path.

edge: Instantiate each allowed building-block category from a module and interface.
negative: Reject a building-block instantiation inside a primitive.
positive: Instantiate a checker inside a program and another checker.

edge: Also explicitly instantiate another module and verify that this rule does not create an additional implicit top for it.
positive: Elaborate one uninstantiated module and one uninstantiated program and observe one top-level instance of each.

edge: Use nested includes and verify all included text belongs to the outer file's compilation unit.
positive: Include a file declaring a compilation-unit item and reference it later in the including unit.

edge: Chain an incomplete declaration across more than two files.
negative: Omit the completing text and diagnose the incomplete declaration.
positive: Split a module declaration across successive files and compile them as the extended unit.

edge: Verify hierarchical paths include each created instance level.
positive: Instantiate a child module and interface and observe the additional instance hierarchy level.

edge: Pass the same interface instance through an interface port and select a member at the receiving instance.
positive: Connect one interface instance to module and program interface ports and select its component signals through each port.

edge: Use interface member subroutines and processes together in one interface instance.
positive: Declare each permitted data, type, subroutine, process, and continuous-assignment category in an interface.

edge: Use the same local identifier spelling in a module and a checker.
positive: Declare the same local identifier independently in two sibling modules without conflict.

edge: Place the initial definition and redefinition in different files of one compilation unit and vary their input order.
positive: Redefine a macro and observe the new replacement only in source text following the redefinition.

edge: Use a macro later in another file that belongs to the same compilation unit.
positive: Use the same spelling for a text macro and a language identifier without a namespace conflict.

edge: Check multiple top-level elements across compilation units.
negative: Combine one explicitly timed design element with another having no specified unit or precision.
positive: Give every design element an explicit or directive-derived time specification.

edge: Expose different interface subroutine sets through two modports.
negative: Reject a module call to an interface subroutine excluded by its modport.
positive: Call an interface subroutine made available to a module through its modport.

edge: Provide opposite modport direction views of the same interface signals to two modules.
negative: Reject a module drive through a modport member that is input from that module's view.
positive: Connect a module through a modport and observe each signal direction from that module's view.

edge: Reuse a member name in a separate enclosing construct's namespace.
negative: Declare a variable and task with the same name in one module namespace.
positive: Use distinct names for members of each listed declaration category in one enclosing construct.

edge: Use a module and a program as simultaneous top-level blocks.
positive: Elaborate two independent top-level modules in one design.

edge: Exercise the explicit port-name completion exception.
negative: Redeclare a variable name in the same scope and namespace.
positive: Use the same spelling in distinct namespaces.

edge: Contrast package ordering with mutually referenced design elements allowed by normal order independence.
negative: Place a package-item reference before compilation of that package.
positive: Compile a package before a source unit importing and referencing its item.

negative: Redeclare the same package name in another unit.
positive: Declare uniquely named packages in separate units.

edge: Contrast an imported package name with an unimported declaration that is not introduced as a local unqualified name.
positive: Import a package declaration into a module and into another package.

edge: Include ordinary compilation-unit-scope declarations that source-language names cannot access cross-unit, while confirming that their compilation units remain traversable through the PLI.
notes: This is an API-facing oracle independent of source-language cross-unit name visibility.
positive: Use the standard PLI compilation-unit iterator to traverse a design containing two compilation units and observe both units.

edge: Exercise input, output, inout, and ref port kinds.
positive: Declare a port and complete it with a same-name net or variable declaration in the module namespace.

edge: Check each prohibited instance category independently.
negative: Reject a program containing an always procedure or a module, interface, primitive, or nested program instance.
positive: Compile a program containing data, a class, a task, an object, initial, and final procedures.

edge: Combine a program with a clocking block and verify race-free sampled/driven design-testbench interaction.
notes: Avoid depending on nondeterministic ordering among processes within one region.
positive: Have module and program processes respond in the same time slot and observe program reactive-region ordering.

edge: Use the same declaration name in a program and an enclosing compilation-unit scope and verify that the scopes remain distinct.
positive: Declare program data and a task in a program and reference them through the program scope.

edge: Use step as a delay unit while confirming it remains illegal as a scope time setting.
negative: Reject step in a timeunit or timeprecision declaration.
positive: Use a physical time unit in a timeunit and timeprecision declaration.

edge: Change the design's finest precision and observe the corresponding step duration.
positive: Use a step delay and observe that it equals one global-precision quantum.

edge: Define a task with no arguments and another using all four directions.
positive: Define and call tasks using each of input, output, inout, and ref arguments.

edge: Contrast a zero-time task with a task that advances simulation time.
positive: Call a task containing a timing control and observe exit at a later simulation time.

edge: Call a task with no arguments and ignore no return value.
negative: Reject use of a task call as an expression operand.
positive: Call a task as a procedural statement.

edge: Nest a module under an enclosing module while a conflicting preceding `timescale and compilation-unit declaration exist.
positive: Construct scopes exercising each fallback level and verify the selected unit and precision.

edge: Use the combined and separate forms in different design elements.
negative: Reject a non-time-literal declaration value.
positive: Declare timeunit 100ps; timeprecision 10fs; and equivalently timeunit 100ps/10fs.

edge: Use equal time unit and precision.
negative: Reject timeunit 1ns with timeprecision 1us.
positive: Use timeunit 1ns with timeprecision 1ps.

edge: Apply the same rules at compilation-unit scope and in each listed design element.
negative: Reject conflicting repetitions or an initial declaration after another scope item.
positive: Place timeunit/timeprecision first and repeat identical declarations later.

edge: Use equal unit and precision, then a finer precision, and compare represented delays.
positive: Declare a time unit and precision and observe delay scaling and accuracy.

edge: Exercise the largest 100s unit and smallest 1fs unit and compare equivalent scaled delays.
negative: Reject an unlisted time suffix or magnitude.
positive: Use each listed suffix with allowed magnitudes in timeunit/timeprecision declarations.

edge: Compare equal unit/precision integer rounding and two elements with different precisions.
positive: With 1ns/100ps, observe a 2.75ns delay rounded to 2.8ns.

edge: Reorder files in one compilation unit and observe the inherited default change for an element without local declarations.
positive: Place two modules after one `timescale and verify both inherit it; replace it before a third.

edge: Vary whitespace around the slash while preserving the required form.
negative: Reject a `timescale directive missing its precision or slash separator.
positive: Specify a valid time unit and precision with the slash-separated `timescale form.

edge: Use $unit:: from a nested task and module scope.
negative: Reject $unit:: selection of a name absent from the current compilation unit.
positive: Shadow a compilation-unit variable locally and select the outer declaration with $unit::.

edge: Remove candidates successively to exercise compilation-unit and hierarchy fallback.
positive: Provide candidates at all three levels and verify the nested declaration wins.
